Brook Estifanos Assignment 6 Text Mining

Exploring Joyful Language in Jane Austen’s Emma using Tidytext

Task 1: Data Preparation

Explanation

I used the notes provided in class to group austen_books by book, detect chapter boundaries using regex and create two new columns linenumber and chapter using dplyr ’s mutate function. I then checked if the work is correct by getting a summary of the number of chapters in each book and comparing it tho the known number of chapters. I felt that the ungroup() was unnecessary in this session because i create a new object based on the

library(janeaustenr)

#1._____Group, detect chpater boundries using regex, create new columns_____

austen_1 <- austen_books() |>
  #makes row_number() restart at 1 for every novel
  group_by(book) |> 
  # creates columens line number and chapter
  mutate(
    linenumber = row_number(),
    #Matches "chapter " + digit or Roman numeral (i,v,x,l,c)
    #cum_sum adds up the TRUE values
    chapter    = cumsum(str_detect(text,
                                   regex("^chapter [\\divxlc]", 
                                         ignore_case = TRUE))) 
  )|> 
  ungroup()  
austen_1

Task 2: Tokenization

Explanation

I utilized unnest_tokens() function from the tidytext package to tokenize by word. I dplyr’s mutate along with strngrs str_extract to create a new column for the words. Finally, dplyr’s anti-join was used to weed out low value words by comparing the text to tidytext’s stop_words dataframe. Without the stop_words there were 216385 total words and 13464 unique ones.

#1.___________Tokenize words using unnest__________

austen_2 <- austen_1 |>
  unnest_tokens(word, text) |> 
  # use str_extract to get just the words inside any format encoding
  mutate(word = str_extract(word, "[a-z']+")) |>
  # filter out words in stop_words
  anti_join(stop_words, by = "word")
austen_2

Task 3: Sentiment Analysis

I used dplyr`s to filter joy words from the three sentiemnt lexicons with their corresponding string arguments nrc (joy), afinn (positive scores ≥ 1), bing (positive)

Explanation 2: Analysis and Visualization

For each of the filtered lexicons I followed the steps below complete this step.

  1. Count word frequency by filtering for the book EMMA, inner joining with the appropriate “joy filtered” sentiment lexicon and counting the resulting word frequency.

  2. Filtering for the top 50 words.

  3. Visualizing by creating a barchart with ggplot’s geom_col, reordered by frequency and a word cloud using the wordcloud() package.

The analysis for each sentiment lexicon is below.

NRC

#________nrc join_____________

#1. Count word frequency  
austen_nrc_freq <- austen_2 |>
  filter(book == "Emma") |>
  inner_join(nrc_joy, by = "word",
             relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  count(word, sort = TRUE)

Explanation 3: Bar charts side by side comparison

I felt it would be cool to visually compare the three bar charts side to see the difference between the kinds of “joy words” matched with each lexicon so I used facet wrap to put them side by side. It was fascinating that the words happy and love occupy spots in the top 3 in all three sentiment lexicons while each lexicon has its own number 1 “joy word”.

#________________all bars in 1 go_______________


# 1. Combine all three lexicons into one lookup table
all_joy_lexicons <- bind_rows(
  nrc_joy   |> select(word) |> mutate(lexicon = "NRC"),
  affin_joy |> select(word) |> mutate(lexicon = "AFINN"),
  bing_joy  |> select(word) |> mutate(lexicon = "Bing")
)

# 2. Count word frequency and filter (n >= 50) across all lexicons at once
austen_all_filter <- austen_2 |>
  filter(book == "Emma") |>
  inner_join(all_joy_lexicons, by = "word", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  count(lexicon, word, sort = TRUE) |>
  filter(n > 50) 

# 3a. Combined bar chart using facet_wrap
austen_all_bar <- austen_all_filter |>
  mutate(word = reorder_within(word, n, lexicon)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = word, fill = lexicon)) +
  geom_col(colour = "black", show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ lexicon, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_reordered() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("NRC" = "steelblue", "AFINN" = "orange", "Bing" = "purple")) +
  labs(
    y = NULL,
    x = "Word Frequency",
    title = "Frequent Joy/Positive Words in Emma by Sentiment Lexicon (n > 50)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

austen_all_bar
